items.name: B-tree
items.summary: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multicolumn indexes. Up to 32 columns can be specified. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: The complete CREATE INDEX synopsis has no INCLUDE clause in this manual build.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

description: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：

original_text./versions/10/capabilities/0/note: Ordinary sorted output is distinct from ordering by an operator, such as nearest-neighbor distance.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/1/note: This means a unique index. Exclusion constraints use a different contract.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/2/note: Multiple search keys are distinct from non-key INCLUDE payload columns.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/3/note: Payload columns do not become search keys. Wide payloads can exceed the index tuple-size limit.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/4/note: The query must use covered values; visibility-map state determines whether heap visits can be avoided.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/5/note: Availability depends on the chosen operator class and ordering operator.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/6/note: A cooperating scan of one index is distinct from a parallel bitmap heap scan or separate serial scans under Parallel Append.
original_text./versions/10/capabilities/7/note: Parallel construction is separate from parallel scans. Worker availability, settings and build phases also matter.
original_text./versions/10/description/0: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/10/sections/0/blocks/0/paragra: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/10/sections/0/blocks/2/paragra: Constructs equivalent to combinations of these operators, such as BETWEEN and IN , can also be implemented with a B-tree index search. Also, an IS NULL or IS NOT NULL condition on an index column can be used with a B-tree index.
original_text./versions/10/sections/0/blocks/3/paragra: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo' , but not col LIKE '%bar' . However, if your database does not use the C locale you will need to create the index with a special operator class to support indexing of pattern-matching queries; see Section 11.9 below. It is also possible to use B-tree indexes for ILIKE and ~* , but only if the pattern starts with non-alphabetic characters, i.e., characters that are not affected by upper/lower case conversion.
original_text./versions/10/sections/0/blocks/4/paragra: B-tree indexes can also be used to retrieve data in sorted order. This is not always faster than a simple scan and sort, but it is often helpful.
original_text./versions/10/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index build, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to gradual degradation in the index's efficiency. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected. If the table is static then fillfactor 100 is best to minimize the index's physical size, but for heavily updated tables a smaller fillfactor is better to minimize the need for page splits. The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

paragraphs: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：
等价于这些运算符组合的表达式，例如 BETWEEN 和 IN，也可通过 B-tree 索引搜索实现。索引列上的 IS NULL 或 IS NOT NULL 条件也能使用 B-tree 索引。

如果模式是常量且锚定于字符串开头，优化器也可为涉及模式匹配运算符 LIKE 和 ~ 的查询使用 B-tree 索引，例如 col LIKE 'foo%' 或 col ~ '^foo'，而非 col LIKE '%bar'。但如果数据库不使用 C 区域设置，需要使用特殊操作符类创建索引，才能支持模式匹配查询；参见下方第 11.9 节。ILIKE 和 ~* 也可能使用 B-tree 索引，但仅限模式以非字母字符开头，即不受大小写转换影响的字符。
B-tree 索引也可按排序顺序检索数据。这不总是比直接扫描后排序更快，但通常有帮助。

10.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING btree (column_name);

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。

evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multiple-key-column indexes. Whether there can be multiple key columns is independent of whether INCLUDE columns can be added to the index. Indexes can have up to 32 columns, including INCLUDE columns. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, the B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST index access methods support this feature. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, only B-tree), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

description: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：

original_text./versions/15/capabilities/0/note: Ordinary sorted output is distinct from ordering by an operator, such as nearest-neighbor distance.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/1/note: This means a unique index. Exclusion constraints use a different contract.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/2/note: Multiple search keys are distinct from non-key INCLUDE payload columns.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/3/note: Payload columns do not become search keys. Wide payloads can exceed the index tuple-size limit.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/4/note: The query must use covered values; visibility-map state determines whether heap visits can be avoided.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/5/note: Availability depends on the chosen operator class and ordering operator.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/6/note: A cooperating scan of one index is distinct from a parallel bitmap heap scan or separate serial scans under Parallel Append.
original_text./versions/15/capabilities/7/note: Parallel construction is separate from parallel scans. Worker availability, settings and build phases also matter.
original_text./versions/15/description/0: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/15/sections/0/blocks/0/paragra: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/15/sections/0/blocks/2/paragra: Constructs equivalent to combinations of these operators, such as BETWEEN and IN , can also be implemented with a B-tree index search. Also, an IS NULL or IS NOT NULL condition on an index column can be used with a B-tree index.
original_text./versions/15/sections/0/blocks/3/paragra: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo' , but not col LIKE '%bar' . However, if your database does not use the C locale you will need to create the index with a special operator class to support indexing of pattern-matching queries; see Section 11.10 below. It is also possible to use B-tree indexes for ILIKE and ~* , but only if the pattern starts with non-alphabetic characters, i.e., characters that are not affected by upper/lower case conversion.
original_text./versions/15/sections/0/blocks/4/paragra: B-tree indexes can also be used to retrieve data in sorted order. This is not always faster than a simple scan and sort, but it is often helpful.
original_text./versions/15/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 67.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.
original_text./versions/15/storage_options/1/descripti: Controls usage of the B-tree deduplication technique described in Section 67.4.3 . Set to ON or OFF to enable or disable the optimization. (Alternative spellings of ON and OFF are allowed as described in Section 20.1 .) The default is ON .
Turning deduplicate_items off via ALTER INDEX prevents future insertions from triggering deduplication, but does not in itself make existing posting list tuples use the standard tuple representation.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 17.11 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. capabilities.label: 按距离排序

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 17.11 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, B-tree, GIN, and BRIN), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

original_text./versions/19/description/0: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/19/sections/0/blocks/0/paragra: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/19/sections/0/blocks/2/paragra: Constructs equivalent to combinations of these operators, such as BETWEEN and IN , can also be implemented with a B-tree index search. Also, an IS NULL or IS NOT NULL condition on an index column can be used with a B-tree index.
original_text./versions/19/sections/0/blocks/3/paragra: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo' , but not col LIKE '%bar' . However, if your database does not use the C locale you will need to create the index with a special operator class to support indexing of pattern-matching queries; see Section 11.10 below. It is also possible to use B-tree indexes for ILIKE and ~* , but only if the pattern starts with non-alphabetic characters, i.e., characters that are not affected by upper/lower case conversion.

original_text./versions/19/storage_options/0/descripti: Controls how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 65.1.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.
original_text./versions/19/storage_options/1/descripti: Controls usage of the B-tree deduplication technique described in Section 65.1.4.3 . Set to ON or OFF to enable or disable the optimization. (Alternative spellings of ON and OFF are allowed as described in Section 19.1 .) The default is ON .
Turning deduplicate_items off via ALTER INDEX prevents future insertions from triggering deduplication, but does not in itself make existing posting list tuples use the standard tuple representation.

original_text./versions/9.0/sections/0/blocks/0/paragr: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. original_text./versions/9.0/sections/0/blocks/2/paragr: Constructs equivalent to combinations of these operators, such as BETWEEN and IN , can also be implemented with a B-tree index search. Also, an IS NULL or IS NOT NULL condition on an index column can be used with a B-tree index.

paragraphs: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：
等价于这些运算符组合的表达式，例如 BETWEEN 和 IN，也可通过 B-tree 索引搜索实现。索引列上的 IS NULL 或 IS NOT NULL 条件也能使用 B-tree 索引。

如果模式是常量且锚定于字符串开头，优化器也可为涉及模式匹配运算符 LIKE 和 ~ 的查询使用 B-tree 索引，例如 col LIKE 'foo%' 或 col ~ '^foo'，而非 col LIKE '%bar'。但如果数据库不使用 C 区域设置，需要使用特殊操作符类创建索引，才能支持模式匹配查询；参见下方第 11.9 节。ILIKE 和 ~* 也可能使用 B-tree 索引，但仅限模式以非字母字符开头，即不受大小写转换影响的字符。

9.0.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING btree (column_name);

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。
storage_options.name: fillfactor

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.1.24 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

original_text./versions/9.3/description/0: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/9.3/sections/0/blocks/0/paragr: B-trees can handle equality and range queries on data that can be sorted into some ordering. In particular, the PostgreSQL query planner will consider using a B-tree index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using one of these operators:
original_text./versions/9.3/sections/0/blocks/2/paragr: Constructs equivalent to combinations of these operators, such as BETWEEN and IN , can also be implemented with a B-tree index search. Also, an IS NULL or IS NOT NULL condition on an index column can be used with a B-tree index.
original_text./versions/9.3/sections/0/blocks/3/paragr: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo' , but not col LIKE '%bar' . However, if your database does not use the C locale you will need to create the index with a special operator class to support indexing of pattern-matching queries; see Section 11.9 below. It is also possible to use B-tree indexes for ILIKE and ~* , but only if the pattern starts with non-alphabetic characters, i.e., characters that are not affected by upper/lower case conversion.
original_text./versions/9.3/sections/0/blocks/4/paragr: B-tree indexes can also be used to retrieve data in sorted order. This is not always faster than a simple scan and sort, but it is often helpful.
original_text./versions/9.3/storage_options/0/descript: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index build, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to gradual degradation in the index's efficiency. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected. If the table is static then fillfactor 100 is best to minimize the index's physical size, but for heavily updated tables a smaller fillfactor is better to minimize the need for page splits. paragraphs: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：
等价于这些运算符组合的表达式，例如 BETWEEN 和 IN，也可通过 B-tree 索引搜索实现。索引列上的 IS NULL 或 IS NOT NULL 条件也能使用 B-tree 索引。

如果模式是常量且锚定于字符串开头，优化器也可为涉及模式匹配运算符 LIKE 和 ~ 的查询使用 B-tree 索引，例如 col LIKE 'foo%' 或 col ~ '^foo'，而非 col LIKE '%bar'。但如果数据库不使用 C 区域设置，需要使用特殊操作符类创建索引，才能支持模式匹配查询；参见下方第 11.9 节。ILIKE 和 ~* 也可能使用 B-tree 索引，但仅限模式以非字母字符开头，即不受大小写转换影响的字符。
B-tree 索引也可按排序顺序检索数据。这不总是比直接扫描后排序更快，但通常有帮助。

9.3.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING btree (column_name);

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。
storage_options.name: fillfactor

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.4.26 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.4.26 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.4.26 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST and GIN index types support multicolumn indexes. Up to 32 columns can be specified. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.4.26 · sql-createindex

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列

evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

original_text./versions/9.6/sections/0/blocks/3/paragr: The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo' , but not col LIKE '%bar' . However, if your database does not use the C locale you will need to create the index with a special operator class to support indexing of pattern-matching queries; see Section 11.9 below. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index build, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). paragraphs: B-tree 能对可按某种顺序排序的数据执行等值查询和范围查询。具体而言，当索引列参与使用下列运算符之一的比较时，PostgreSQL 查询规划器会考虑使用 B-tree 索引：
等价于这些运算符组合的表达式，例如 BETWEEN 和 IN，也可通过 B-tree 索引搜索实现。索引列上的 IS NULL 或 IS NOT NULL 条件也能使用 B-tree 索引。

如果模式是常量且锚定于字符串开头，优化器也可为涉及模式匹配运算符 LIKE 和 ~ 的查询使用 B-tree 索引，例如 col LIKE 'foo%' 或 col ~ '^foo'，而非 col LIKE '%bar'。但如果数据库不使用 C 区域设置，需要使用特殊操作符类创建索引，才能支持模式匹配查询；参见下方第 11.9 节。ILIKE 和 ~* 也可能使用 B-tree 索引，但仅限模式以非字母字符开头，即不受大小写转换影响的字符。

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。

items.summary: Hash 索引存储从索引列值派生出的 32 位 hash 码。因此，这类索引只能处理简单的等值比较。只要已索引列参与的是使用等号操作符的比较，查询规划器就会考虑使用 Hash 索引：

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 按距离排序

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

description: 索引的填充因子是一个百分比，用于确定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-树，在初始构建索引时，以及在右侧扩展索引（加入新的最大键值）时，叶子页都会填充到这一百分比。如果页面随后变成全满，就会发生分裂，从而导致磁盘上的索引结构碎片化。B-树默认使用 90 的填充因子，但也可以选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数值。

对预计会有大量插入和/或更新的表，在 CREATE INDEX 时为 B-树索引设置较低的填充因子会有好处（即在向表批量装载数据之后）。50 到 90 范围内的值可以有效地 “ 平滑 ” B-树索引生命周期早期页面分裂的 速率 （这样降低填充因子甚至可能减少页面分裂的绝对数量，不过这一效果高度依赖工作负载）。 第 64.4.2 节 中描述的 B-树自底向上索引删除技术依赖于页面上有一些 “ 额外 ” 空间来存储 “ 额外 ” 的元组版本，因此也会受到填充因子影响（不过通常影响不大）。
在某些其他特定情况下，在 CREATE INDEX 时将填充因子提高到 100 可能有助于最大化空间利用率。只有在完全确定该表是静态的（即永远不会受到插入或更新影响）时，才应考虑这样做。否则，将填充因子设为 100 有 损害 性能的风险：即便只有少量更新或插入，也会导致页面突然大量分裂。
其他索引方法以不同但大致类似的方式使用填充因子；默认填充因子因方法而异。

在某些其他特定情况下，在 CREATE INDEX 时将填充因子提高到 100 可能有助于最大化空间利用率。只有在完全确定该表是静态的（即永远不会受到插入或更新影响）时，才应考虑这样做。否则，将填充因子设为 100 有 损害 性能的风险：即便只有少量更新或插入，也会导致页面突然大量分裂。
其他索引方法以不同但大致类似的方式使用填充因子；默认填充因子因方法而异。
storage_options.name: fillfactor

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multiple-key-column indexes. Whether there can be multiple key columns is independent of whether INCLUDE columns can be added to the index. Indexes can have up to 32 columns, including INCLUDE columns. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, the B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST index access methods support this feature. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 16.15 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, only B-tree), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

original_text./versions/16/capabilities/1/note: This means a unique index. Exclusion constraints use a different contract.
original_text./versions/16/capabilities/2/note: Multiple search keys are distinct from non-key INCLUDE payload columns.
original_text./versions/16/capabilities/3/note: Payload columns do not become search keys. Wide payloads can exceed the index tuple-size limit.
original_text./versions/16/capabilities/4/note: The query must use covered values; visibility-map state determines whether heap visits can be avoided.
original_text./versions/16/capabilities/5/note: Availability depends on the chosen operator class and ordering operator.
original_text./versions/16/capabilities/6/note: A cooperating scan of one index is distinct from a parallel bitmap heap scan or separate serial scans under Parallel Append.

The query planner will consider using a hash index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using the equal operator:
original_text./versions/16/sections/0/blocks/0/paragra: Hash indexes store a 32-bit hash code derived from the value of the indexed column. Hence, such indexes can only handle simple equality comparisons. The query planner will consider using a hash index whenever an indexed column is involved in a comparison using the equal operator:
original_text./versions/16/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 67.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

paragraphs: Hash 索引存储从索引列值派生出的 32 位 hash 码。因此，这类索引只能处理简单的等值比较。只要已索引列参与的是使用等号操作符的比较，查询规划器就会考虑使用 Hash 索引：

18.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING hash (column_name);

description: 控制索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-树，在初始构建索引时，以及在右侧扩展索引（加入新的最大键值）时，叶子页都会填充到这一百分比。如果页面随后变成全满，就会发生分裂，从而导致磁盘上的索引结构碎片化。B-树默认使用 90 的填充因子，但也可以选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数值。

对预计会有大量插入和/或更新的表，在 CREATE INDEX 时为 B-树索引设置较低的填充因子会有好处（即在向表批量装载数据之后）。50 到 90 范围内的值可以有效地 “ 平滑 ” B-树索引生命周期早期页面分裂的 速率 （这样降低填充因子甚至可能减少页面分裂的绝对数量，不过这一效果高度依赖工作负载）。 第 65.1.4.2 节 中描述的 B-树自底向上索引删除技术依赖于页面上有一些 “ 额外 ” 空间来存储 “ 额外 ” 的元组版本，因此也会受到填充因子影响（不过通常影响不大）。
在某些其他特定情况下，在 CREATE INDEX 时将填充因子提高到 100 可能有助于最大化空间利用率。只有在完全确定该表是静态的（即永远不会受到插入或更新影响）时，才应考虑这样做。否则，将填充因子设为 100 有 损害 性能的风险：即便只有少量更新或插入，也会导致页面突然大量分裂。
其他索引方法以不同但大致类似的方式使用填充因子；默认填充因子因方法而异。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multiple-key-column indexes. Whether there can be multiple key columns is independent of whether INCLUDE columns can be added to the index. Indexes can have up to 32 columns, including INCLUDE columns. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, the B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST index access methods support this feature. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, B-tree, GIN, and BRIN), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

paragraphs: Hash 索引只能处理简单等值比较。当索引列参与使用 = 运算符的比较时，查询规划器会考虑使用 Hash 索引。以下命令用于创建 Hash 索引：

blocks.code: CREATE INDEX name ON table USING hash (column);

paragraphs: 此版本的 Hash 索引操作尚不记录 WAL，因此数据库崩溃时若有尚未写入的变更，可能需要通过 REINDEX 重建 Hash 索引。此外，初始基础备份之后的 Hash 索引变化不会通过流复制或基于文件的复制传播，因此后续使用这些索引的查询会得到错误结果。基于这些原因，此版本不建议使用 Hash 索引。

9.0.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING hash (column_name);

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。
storage_options.name: fillfactor

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multicolumn indexes. Up to 32 columns can be specified. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree index access method supports this feature. In B-tree indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 11.22 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, only B-tree), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

original_text./versions/14/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, only B-tree), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

original_text./versions/15/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 67.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

description: 索引的填充因子是一个百分比，用于确定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-树，在初始构建索引时，以及在右侧扩展索引（加入新的最大键值）时，叶子页都会填充到这一百分比。如果页面随后变成全满，就会发生分裂，从而导致磁盘上的索引结构碎片化。B-树默认使用 90 的填充因子，但也可以选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数值。

evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. evidence.label: PostgreSQL 17.11 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 17.11 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, B-tree and BRIN), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

original_text./versions/17/storage_options/0/descripti: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 64.1.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.
The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 19beta4 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). description: 控制索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-树，在初始构建索引时，以及在右侧扩展索引（加入新的最大键值）时，叶子页都会填充到这一百分比。如果页面随后变成全满，就会发生分裂，从而导致磁盘上的索引结构碎片化。B-树默认使用 90 的填充因子，但也可以选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数值。

original_text./versions/9.0/storage_options/0/descript: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index build, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to gradual degradation in the index's efficiency. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected. If the table is static then fillfactor 100 is best to minimize the index's physical size, but for heavily updated tables a smaller fillfactor is better to minimize the need for page splits. The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 9.1.24 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

original_text./versions/9.6/sections/0/blocks/2/paragr: (See Section 9.11 for the meaning of these operators.) original_text./versions/9.6/sections/0/blocks/3/paragr: GiST indexes are also capable of optimizing "nearest-neighbor" searches, such as
original_text./versions/9.6/sections/0/blocks/5/paragr: which finds the ten places closest to a given target point. The ability to do this is again dependent on the particular operator class being used. In Table 61-1 , operators that can be used in this way are listed in the column "Ordering Operators" .
original_text./versions/9.6/storage_options/0/descript: The fillfactor for an index is a percentage that determines how full the index method will try to pack index pages. For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index build, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to gradual degradation in the index's efficiency. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected. If the table is static then fillfactor 100 is best to minimize the index's physical size, but for heavily updated tables a smaller fillfactor is better to minimize the need for page splits. The other index methods use fillfactor in different but roughly analogous ways; the default fillfactor varies between methods.
original_text./versions/9.6/storage_options/1/descript: Determines whether the buffering build technique described in Section 61.4.1 is used to build the index. With OFF it is disabled, with ON it is enabled, and with AUTO it is initially disabled, but turned on on-the-fly once the index size reaches effective_cache_size . The default is AUTO .

（这些运算符的含义参见第 9.11 节。） 标准发行版中的 GiST 操作符类见表 61-1。 contrib 集合或独立项目中还提供许多其他 GiST 操作符类。 更多信息参见第 61 章。
GiST 索引还可以优化近邻搜索，例如：

blocks.code: SELECT * FROM places ORDER BY location <-> point '(101,456)' LIMIT 10;

paragraphs: 该查询找出距离指定目标点最近的十个地点。能否进行这种查询仍取决于使用的具体操作符类。表 61-1 的“排序运算符（Ordering Operators）”列中列出了可以这样使用的运算符。

description: 索引的 fillfactor 是一个百分比，决定索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-tree，首次构建索引和从右侧扩展索引（添加新的最大键值）时，叶页会填充到该比例。页面之后若完全填满，就会分裂，使索引效率逐渐降低。B-tree 的默认 fillfactor 为 90，可选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数。如果表是静态的，使用 100 最有利于缩小索引的物理大小；频繁更新的表则适合较小的 fillfactor，以减少页面分裂。其他索引方法使用 fillfactor 的方式不同，但大致类似；默认值因方法而异。

items.summary: SP-GiST 与 GiST 一样，提供支持多种搜索方式的基础框架。SP-GiST 可实现多种基于磁盘的非平衡数据结构，例如四叉树、k-d 树和基数树（tries）。例如，PostgreSQL 标准发行版提供二维点的 SP-GiST 操作符类，支持使用下列运算符的索引查询：

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multicolumn indexes. Up to 32 columns can be specified. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: The complete CREATE INDEX synopsis has no INCLUDE clause in this manual build.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 10.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

capabilities.label: 并行构建索引
capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 13.23 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multiple-key-column indexes. Whether there can be multiple key columns is independent of whether INCLUDE columns can be added to the index. Indexes can have up to 32 columns, including INCLUDE columns. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, the B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST index access methods support this feature. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · indexes-types
evidence.quote: Like GiST, SP-GiST supports “ nearest-neighbor ” searches. For SP-GiST operator classes that support distance ordering, the corresponding operator is listed in the “ Ordering Operators ” column in Table 69.1 .

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 15.19 · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, only B-tree), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 18.6 · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 18.6 · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

For B-trees, leaf pages are filled to this percentage during initial index builds, and also when extending the index at the right (adding new largest key values). If pages subsequently become completely full, they will be split, leading to fragmentation of the on-disk index structure. B-trees use a default fillfactor of 90, but any integer value from 10 to 100 can be selected.

B-tree indexes on tables where many inserts and/or updates are anticipated can benefit from lower fillfactor settings at CREATE INDEX time (following bulk loading into the table). Values in the range of 50 - 90 can usefully “ smooth out ” the rate of page splits during the early life of the B-tree index (lowering fillfactor like this may even lower the absolute number of page splits, though this effect is highly workload dependent). The B-tree bottom-up index deletion technique described in Section 65.1.4.2 is dependent on having some “ extra ” space on pages to store “ extra ” tuple versions, and so can be affected by fillfactor (though the effect is usually not significant).

In other specific cases it might be useful to increase fillfactor to 100 at CREATE INDEX time as a way of maximizing space utilization. You should only consider this when you are completely sure that the table is static (i.e. that it will never be affected by either inserts or updates). A fillfactor setting of 100 otherwise risks harming performance: even a few updates or inserts will cause a sudden flood of page splits.

（这些操作符的含义见 第 9.11 节 。）标准发布版自带的 SP-GiST 操作符类记录在 表 65.2 中。更多信息见 第 65.3 节 。

19.signature: CREATE INDEX name ON table_name USING spgist (column_name);

description: 控制索引方法尝试将索引页填充到多满。对于 B-树，在初始构建索引时，以及在右侧扩展索引（加入新的最大键值）时，叶子页都会填充到这一百分比。如果页面随后变成全满，就会发生分裂，从而导致磁盘上的索引结构碎片化。B-树默认使用 90 的填充因子，但也可以选择 10 到 100 之间的任意整数值。

对预计会有大量插入和/或更新的表，在 CREATE INDEX 时为 B-树索引设置较低的填充因子会有好处（即在向表批量装载数据之后）。50 到 90 范围内的值可以有效地 “ 平滑 ” B-树索引生命周期早期页面分裂的 速率 （这样降低填充因子甚至可能减少页面分裂的绝对数量，不过这一效果高度依赖工作负载）。 第 65.1.4.2 节 中描述的 B-树自底向上索引删除技术依赖于页面上有一些 “ 额外 ” 空间来存储 “ 额外 ” 的元组版本，因此也会受到填充因子影响（不过通常影响不大）。
在某些其他特定情况下，在 CREATE INDEX 时将填充因子提高到 100 可能有助于最大化空间利用率。只有在完全确定该表是静态的（即永远不会受到插入或更新影响）时，才应考虑这样做。否则，将填充因子设为 100 有 损害 性能的风险：即便只有少量更新或插入，也会导致页面突然大量分裂。
其他索引方法以不同但大致类似的方式使用填充因子；默认填充因子因方法而异。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · indexes-ordering
evidence.quote: In addition to simply finding the rows to be returned by a query, an index may be able to deliver them in a specific sorted order. This allows a query's ORDER BY specification to be honored without a separate sorting step. Of the index types currently supported by PostgreSQL , only B-tree can produce sorted output — the other index types return matching rows in an unspecified, implementation-dependent order.

capabilities.label: 有序输出
capabilities.note: 普通的有序输出与按运算符排序是不同能力，例如按近邻距离排序。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · indexes-unique
evidence.quote: Currently, only B-tree indexes can be declared unique.

capabilities.label: 唯一键
capabilities.note: 这里指唯一索引，排除约束采用不同的约定。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · indexes-multicolumn
evidence.quote: Currently, only the B-tree, GiST, GIN, and BRIN index types support multiple-key-column indexes. Whether there can be multiple key columns is independent of whether INCLUDE columns can be added to the index. Indexes can have up to 32 columns, including INCLUDE columns. (This limit can be altered when building PostgreSQL ; see the file pg_config_manual.h .)

capabilities.label: 多键列
capabilities.note: 多个检索键与不参与检索的 INCLUDE 附加列是不同概念。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: Currently, the B-tree, GiST and SP-GiST index access methods support this feature. In these indexes, the values of columns listed in the INCLUDE clause are included in leaf tuples which correspond to heap tuples, but are not included in upper-level index entries used for tree navigation.

capabilities.label: INCLUDE 附加列
capabilities.note: 附加列不会成为检索键。过宽的附加数据可能超过索引元组大小限制。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · indexes-index-only-scans
evidence.quote: The index type must support index-only scans. B-tree indexes always do. GiST and SP-GiST indexes support index-only scans for some operator classes but not others. Other index types have no support. The underlying requirement is that the index must physically store, or else be able to reconstruct, the original data value for each index entry. As a counterexample, GIN indexes cannot support index-only scans because each index entry typically holds only part of the original data value.

capabilities.label: 仅索引扫描
capabilities.note: 查询必须使用索引覆盖的值；能否避免访问堆取决于可见性映射状态。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · indexes-types
evidence.quote: Like GiST, SP-GiST supports “ nearest-neighbor ” searches. For SP-GiST operator classes that support distance ordering, the corresponding operator is listed in the “ Ordering Operators ” column in Table 65.2 .

capabilities.label: 按距离排序
capabilities.note: 可用性取决于所选操作符类和排序运算符。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · parallel-plans
evidence.quote: In a parallel index scan or parallel index-only scan , the cooperating processes take turns reading data from the index. Currently, parallel index scans are supported only for btree indexes. Each process will claim a single index block and will scan and return all tuples referenced by that block; other processes can at the same time be returning tuples from a different index block. The results of a parallel btree scan are returned in sorted order within each worker process.

capabilities.label: 并行索引扫描
capabilities.note: 多个进程协作扫描同一索引，不同于并行位图堆扫描，也不同于 Parallel Append 下各自独立的串行扫描。

evidence.label: PostgreSQL 20devel · sql-createindex
evidence.quote: PostgreSQL can build indexes while leveraging multiple CPUs in order to process the table rows faster. This feature is known as parallel index build . For index methods that support building indexes in parallel (currently, B-tree, GIN, and BRIN), maintenance_work_mem specifies the maximum amount of memory that can be used by each index build operation as a whole, regardless of how many worker processes were started. Generally, a cost model automatically determines how many worker processes should be requested, if any.

capabilities.note: 并行构建与并行扫描分别记录，还取决于工作进程是否可用、配置和构建阶段。
